maps.title: Mukunda-mala-stotra · Day 01 · Text 1: Make me a constant reciter

nodeData.topic: Day 01 · Text 1: Make me a constant reciter
nodeData.note: Mukunda-mala-stotra 1 · a class by HH Bhakti Dhira Damodara Swami. King Kulasekhara begs Mukunda, addressing Him by many names, to make him a constant reciter of those names. Maharaj explains that such glorification flows only from pure love, that devotees beg rather than demand, and that remembering the merciful Lord protects and purifies. He closes by warning that service done as routine becomes a burden. Notes are our own summary of the class; tap a bubble's link to hear that moment on YouTube.

children.note:
The class opens a reading of Mukunda-mala-stotra, the prayers of King Kulasekhara, with translation and purport by Srila Prabhupada. This is Text 1, spoken in Mauritius.

🎙 Maharaj at 06:05 (auto-transcript): “A reading from Mukundan Malastutra, a prayers of King Kulaseka, second text one. This text is translated and purported by Divine Grace Sisi Bhaktivedanta Swaham Sule Paupad. Shrivala Deity Vada Deity Dayapareti”

orbit.ref: Mukunda-mālā-stotra: The Prayers of King Kulaśekhara | Text 1 | Mauritius | 5 Dec 2022 · 06:05

children.note:
Kulasekhara calls the Lord by many names — dear to Lakshmi, giver of blessings, causelessly merciful, dear to His devotees, ender of birth and death, resting on the serpent bed — and asks only to become a constant reciter of those names.

🎙 Maharaj at 13:57 (auto-transcript): “O Mukunda, my Lord Please, let me become a constant reciter of your names. Addressing you on Sri Balaba, he who is very dear to Lakshmi, Varada, the best lawyer of the benedictions, Dayapara, he who is costlessly merciful, Bhakta Priya, he who is very dear to his devotees,…”

orbit.ref: Mukunda-mālā-stotra: The Prayers of King Kulaśekhara | Text 1 | Mauritius | 5 Dec 2022 · 13:57

children.note:
Maharaj recalls that in the fourth canto Dhruva Maharaj offered beautiful prayers only after Krishna blessed him. Such prayers are not academic skill or heredity; they come from ecstatic love for Krishna.

🎙 Maharaj at 15:58 (auto-transcript): “In the fourth canto of Bhagavatam, when Krishna tossed Dura Maharaj on his forehead, it is then Dura Maharaj offered beautiful prayers. The Pope of Prophet said, Such prayers are offered when Krishna has given blessing.”

orbit.ref: Mukunda-mālā-stotra: The Prayers of King Kulaśekhara | Text 1 | Mauritius | 5 Dec 2022 · 15:58

children.note:
Devotion is not forced or motivated; it is the natural expression of love. When you like something, you want to glorify it. — “Bhakti is not routine.”

🎙 Maharaj at 18:02 (auto-transcript): “See, there is self of Krishna with affection, routine. Bhakti is not routine. Bhakti is the expression of one's love for Krishna. That is bhakti. Devotion. It's not by force. And it is not motivated by anything. It is prompted by the lovely feelings one have for Krishna. When…”

orbit.ref: Mukunda-mālā-stotra: The Prayers of King Kulaśekhara | Text 1 | Mauritius | 5 Dec 2022 · 18:02

children.note:
An envious person never praises the one he envies, so non-devotees cannot glorify Krishna. A pure devotee's words are perfect and complete, and whoever hears them is purified — that is the sign of real potency. — “So, only pure devotees will have appropriate glorification for Krishna.”

🎙 Maharaj at 18:39 (auto-transcript): “Yes. So, only pure devotees will have appropriate glorification for Krishna. An envious person will never glorify somebody who will be envied. So, non-devotees cannot glorify Krishna because they are envious of Krishna. But pure devotees, they can glorify Krishna…”

orbit.ref: Mukunda-mālā-stotra: The Prayers of King Kulaśekhara | Text 1 | Mauritius | 5 Dec 2022 · 18:39

children.note:
In every book the acaryas offer prayers, give the content, and give blessings — some even give a blessing for every chapter: whoever hears this will surely attain the result.

🎙 Maharaj at 19:25 (auto-transcript): “see in every in every in every of our chariots books there are three things they always do the three things offering prayers they always offer prayers they give us the content or the book and they give blessings this is a formula all throughout and each time backward every…”

orbit.ref: Mukunda-mālā-stotra: The Prayers of King Kulaśekhara | Text 1 | Mauritius | 5 Dec 2022 · 19:25

children.note:
Kulasekhara is begging, not demanding. Like all the acaryas, devotees always long for the mercy of the Lord and His devotees to enter the mysteries of bhakti and glorify Krishna constantly. — “He's not demanding, he's begging.”

🎙 Maharaj at 20:25 (auto-transcript): “So Kula Chakra Maharaj is begging, please let me become a constant reciter of your names. He's begging, he's begging. He's not demanding, he's begging. This is the formula we were discussing yesterday. We need the blessing. And you see all our Acharyas, this is the formula.…”

orbit.ref: Mukunda-mālā-stotra: The Prayers of King Kulaśekhara | Text 1 | Mauritius | 5 Dec 2022 · 20:25

children.note:
Glorifying Krishna constantly, not sometimes, and speaking about Him tirelessly, is the very purpose of having a tongue. — “is the purpose of having the tongue”

🎙 Maharaj at 21:28 (auto-transcript): “not sometimes, constantly, always to glorify Lord Krishna is the purpose of having the tongue that's the purpose of having the tongue so glorify Lord Krishna to speak about Krishna tirelessly so he's begging thank you he's begging make me a constant reciter of your name who…”

orbit.ref: Mukunda-mālā-stotra: The Prayers of King Kulaśekhara | Text 1 | Mauritius | 5 Dec 2022 · 21:28

children.note:
Maharaj asks who can pray like this. We cannot keep doing something that is not tasty for long; Kulasekhara prays for chanting because he knows the holy name purifies and is sweet nectar. — “you cannot do it for a long time.”

🎙 Maharaj at 22:02 (auto-transcript): “we cannot do something coach is not tasty for a long time. If it is not tasty, you cannot do it for a long time. If chanting the names of Krishna is not a tasty sweet nectar, he wouldn't waste his time to pray for this. He would pray for something else. He would act for…”

orbit.ref: Mukunda-mālā-stotra: The Prayers of King Kulaśekhara | Text 1 | Mauritius | 5 Dec 2022 · 22:02

children.note:
Maharaj describes Varadaraja in South India, standing with a sign in His palm that says do not be afraid, do not worry. Krishna is always giving out blessings, and the fortunate beg Him rather than others.

🎙 Maharaj at 23:01 (auto-transcript): “Varada, who is the bestoyer of benediction. We have Varada Raj in South India. Varada Raj. He gives blessings to whoever comes there. He stands like this. And in the palm, Mahasuchara is written there. Mahasuchara. Don't be afraid. Don't worry. Don't hesitate. Don't ever…”

orbit.ref: Mukunda-mālā-stotra: The Prayers of King Kulaśekhara | Text 1 | Mauritius | 5 Dec 2022 · 23:01

children.note:
Seeking blessings from people can be dangerous; real blessings never implicate us, they lift us up. — “Blessings cannot be dangerous.”

🎙 Maharaj at 24:07 (auto-transcript): “Blessings cannot be dangerous. Blessings cannot be implicating. Blessings are elevating. So Christian gives blessings. He is a bestseller of blessings to those who are preaching. Christian is always giving out. And Mathura Alokasana came to Mathura and he made a florist.…”

🎙 Maharaj at 24:33 (auto-transcript): “And Mathura Alokasana came to Mathura and he made a florist. Krishna blessed him. You go back to my abode. This lifetime, you go back and you have my opulence. We should constantly beg Krishna for pure devotion, love, attachment, service and above all remembrance — I don't want to see, hear or do anything else; let it be You. — “I want to constantly remember you.”

In the last prayer of the book Kulasekhara asks that wherever his mind, eyes and senses go, he sees only Krishna. History shows how powerful remembering Him is.

🎙 Maharaj at 26:27 (auto-transcript): “Biba Bangalata, in the last prayer, after he finished all the prayer, this is the end. 🎙 Maharaj at 33:26 (auto-transcript): “Jagandivas are the result of the cosmos. And Lord Krishna lie on the bed of an artist. That is the bed of Krishna, his own expansion, his own expansion. nodeData.topic: Day 02 · Text 2: Victory to Devaki's son
nodeData.note: Mukunda-mala-stotra 2 · a class by HH Bhakti Dhira Damodara Swami. Kulasekhara hails Krishna again and again as the son of Devaki, the light of the Vrishni dynasty, dark and soft like a new cloud, and Mukunda who lifts the earth's burden. Maharaj explains how the father of all can have a mother and father, why Krishna is both greatest and smallest, why He descends, and why Nanda and Yashoda are His real parents. In the questions he shows how Krishna personally protects and provides for those who depend on Him. Notes are our own summary of the class; tap a bubble's link to hear that moment on YouTube.

nodeData.topic: Day 03 · Text 3: Never forget Your lotus feet
nodeData.note: Mukunda-mala-stotra 3 · a class by HH Bhakti Dhira Damodara Swami. Bowing his head, Kulasekhara asks Mukunda for just one blessing: to remember His lotus feet in every future birth. Maharaj calls the material world a phantasmagoria we cannot fix, urges us to change ourselves and use this body to gain a spiritual one, and shows through Prahlada, Advaita, Murari Gupta, Lakshmana and Sita that pure devotees ask only for service. The questions cover juggling services, praying to demigods and caring for the body. Notes are our own summary of the class; tap a bubble's link to hear that moment on YouTube.

nodeData.topic: Day 04 · Text 4: Only to remember You
nodeData.note: Mukunda-mala-stotra 4 · a class by HH Bhakti Dhira Damodara Swami. Kulasekhara says he prays to Hari's lotus feet not to escape hell or to enjoy heaven, but only to remember Him in the core of his heart, birth after birth. Maharaj explains how such remembrance makes a devotee indifferent to this world, why pure devotees are never deluded, and how faith in Krishna should only deepen under trial. He closes with Kholaveca Sridhara's contentment and a warning about offences. Notes are our own summary of the class; tap a bubble's link to hear that moment on YouTube.

nodeData.topic: Day 05 · Text 5: Only Unflinching Devotion, Birth After Birth
nodeData.note: Mukunda-mala-stotra 5 · a class by HH Bhakti Dhira Damodara Swami. King Kulasekhara says he has no attachment to religiosity, wealth or sense enjoyment, which will come anyway by karma, and asks only for steady devotion to the Lord's lotus feet in every birth. Maharaj contrasts this with blind tradition, temple-going for favours and charity done for heaven or for one's name, and explains why it is wiser to approach Krishna, who purifies before he gives, than the demigods. Notes are our own summary of the class; tap a bubble's link to hear that moment on YouTube.

nodeData.topic: Day 06 · Text 6: Anywhere, If I Remember You
nodeData.note: Mukunda-mala-stotra 6 · a class by HH Bhakti Dhira Damodara Swami. King Kulasekhara tells the Lord he will live among demigods, humans or even in hell as the Lord wishes, if only he can remember the Lord's lotus feet at death. Maharaj tells how Narakasura gathered the queens Krishna married, explains that faith and remembrance must keep growing because death tests everything, and contrasts Krishna's ever-new beauty and transcendental senses with anything material. He closes by warning that falldown comes from deviation and bad association. Notes are our own summary of the class; tap a bubble's link to hear that moment on YouTube.

nodeData.topic: Day 07 · Text 7: Always Thinking of Joyful Hari
nodeData.note: Mukunda-mala-stotra 7 · a class by HH Bhakti Dhira Damodara Swami. King Kulasekhara says he always thinks of Hari, the ever-joyful Lord who appears as the son of Nanda and is worshipped by sages like Narada. Maharaj explains that we live a life dictated by the senses and find real happiness only by joining the ever-blissful Lord, taking shelter as Narottama dasa Thakura does with Nityananda, and he describes how the gopis' love makes the Lord of Vaikuntha dance. In the questions he gives signs of chanting properly. Notes are our own summary of the class; tap a bubble's link to hear that moment on YouTube.

nodeData.topic: Day 08 · Text 8: Diving into Hari's Lake
nodeData.note: Mukunda-mala-stotra 8 · a class by HH Bhakti Dhira Damodara Swami. Worn out by the desert of material life, King Kulasekhara resolves to dive into the lake of Lord Hari's beauty, where the lotuses are his hands and feet and the fish his eyes. Maharaj explains that only devotional service relieves this exhaustion, that we hold back through ignorance and doubt, and that even a drop of devotion is enough; he tells of a lady on a train who refused five blessings. In the questions he speaks on faith and hearing, Rukmini's attraction to Krishna, and why devotees avoid onion and garlic. Notes are our own summary of the class; tap a bubble's link to hear that moment on YouTube.

nodeData.topic: Day 09 · Text 9: Never Stop Relishing Murari's Feet
nodeData.note: Mukunda-mala-stotra 9 · a class by HH Bhakti Dhira Damodara Swami. King Kulasekhara tells his mind never to stop relishing thoughts of Murari's lotus feet, and Maharaj explains that real pleasure is not of this world and that the way to remember Krishna constantly is continuous hearing in devotee association. Through the story of Murasura he warns against bad association, then speaks on modern distractions, which austerity is condemned, and how responsible parents like Saci Mata and Jagannath Misra train their children. Notes are our own summary of the class; tap a bubble's link to hear that moment on YouTube.

children.note:

maps.title: Mukunda-mala-stotra · Day 10 · Text 10: Mind, Do Not Fear Yamaraj

nodeData.topic: Day 10 · Text 10: Mind, Do Not Fear Yamaraj
nodeData.note: Mukunda-mala-stotra 10 · a class by HH Bhakti Dhira Damodara Swami. King Kulasekhara tells his mind to stop fearing Yamaraj and its own sins, since its master is Narayana, who can do anything for his servant. Maharaj teaches that fear is a warning that we are not doing our part, that Krishna is eager to give his devotees everything, and that bhakti and the Holy Name burn up a sincere devotee's reactions, with pastimes of Mahaprabhu and questions on material desires and trials. Notes are our own summary of the class; tap a bubble's link to hear that moment on YouTube.

children.note:
Kulasekhara scolds his foolish mind for fretting over Yamaraj's punishments and its own sins: its master is Narayana, husband of the goddess of fortune, easily reached by devotion, so what can he not do for his servant? Maharaj asks the assembly if they are convinced.

🎙 Maharaj at 09:42 (auto-transcript): “Nabi, Mabihi, do not be afraid, manda, foolish, mona, oh mind, vichintia, thinking, bahudha, The Lord of Death, long-lasting, about the torments, not, ever, indeed.”

orbit.ref: Mukunda-mālā-stotra: The Prayers of King Kulaśekhara | Text 10 | December 20, 2022 · 09:42

nodeData.topic: Day 11 · Text 11: Vishnu, the Only Boat
nodeData.note: Mukunda-mala-stotra 11 · a class by HH Bhakti Dhira Damodara Swami. King Kulasekhara describes people drowning in the ocean of birth and death, worn out by family burdens, with Lord Vishnu as the only boat. Maharaj illustrates it with a neglected mother in Mauritius, Prahlada's teachings, Gajendra and Citraketu, and turns the mirror on devotees: false ego, impersonal dealings, the guru's wish for a pure devotee, and depression as a soul starved of the Holy Name. Notes are our own summary of the class; tap a bubble's link to hear that moment on YouTube.

nodeData.topic: Day 12 · Text 12: Grant Me Devotion's Boat
nodeData.note: Mukunda-mala-stotra 12 · a class by HH Bhakti Dhira Damodara Swami. King Kulasekhara describes samsara as an ocean of hankering whipped up by lust, with our own relatives as its sharks, and begs for the boat of devotion. Maharaj shows how desire begets desire, that bhakti is given by mercy and not acquired by strength, and, with stories from Nigeria, New Delhi and a hospital, why we must prepare for death and thank Krishna every day. Notes are our own summary of the class; tap a bubble's link to hear that moment on YouTube.

maps.title: Mukunda-mala-stotra · Day 13 · Text 14: All greatness shrinks before Him

nodeData.topic: Day 13 · Text 14: All greatness shrinks before Him
nodeData.note: Mukunda-mala-stotra 14 · a class by HH Bhakti Dhira Damodara Swami. Once the Lord is seen, everything this world calls great looks tiny, and Maharaj explains that this is the natural experience of pure devotees, not an insult to anyone. He shows how senior Vaishnavas act beyond the body, tells the story of Narada searching for what is greatest, and urges steady sadhana and gratitude. Questions bring out that real renunciation is opulence. Notes are our own summary of the class; tap a bubble's link to hear that moment on YouTube.

nodeData.topic: Day 14 · Text 17: Serve only the greatest master
nodeData.note: Mukunda-mala-stotra 17 · a class by HH Bhakti Dhira Damodara Swami. Kulasekhara laments that we leave Narayana, who shares his own kingdom with his servants, to beg favours from petty masters. Maharaj contrasts the anxiety of material opulence with the opulences of Vaikuntha, shows that real equality with the Lord is personal, and retells the story of the man who kept searching for the greatest master. Questions cover what it really means to know Krishna as supreme, how deities hear us, and why strict chanters can stay harsh. Notes are our own summary of the class; tap a bubble's link to hear that moment on YouTube.

maps.title: Mukunda-mala-stotra · Day 15 · Text 15: The holy name as medicine

nodeData.topic: Day 15 · Text 15: The holy name as medicine
nodeData.note: Mukunda-mala-stotra 15 · a class by HH Bhakti Dhira Damodara Swami. Kulasekhara calls Krishna's name the medicine for the disease of birth and death, and Maharaj explains how to drink it: chant with the tongue and hear with the ears, with full attention and no worry. Pariksit's seven days, Kulasekhara marching his army into the sea, and the crowd that crossed the river for Caitanya Mahaprabhu all show what real absorption does. Notes are our own summary of the class; tap a bubble's link to hear that moment on YouTube.

maps.title: Mukunda-mala-stotra · Day 16 · Text 18: Tears while meditating on His feet

nodeData.topic: Day 16 · Text 18: Tears while meditating on His feet
nodeData.note: Mukunda-mala-stotra 18 · a class by HH Bhakti Dhira Damodara Swami. Kulasekhara asks the lotus-eyed Lord to sustain the devotees who relish meditating on his feet with joined palms, bowed heads and tears. Maharaj explains why Krishna's feet are called lotus, why we never have time for Krishna, and why deity worship is worship of a person, never of an idol. Questions cover Jagannatha's kitchen, breaking the habit of running for money, and worship done only as duty. Notes are our own summary of the class; tap a bubble's link to hear that moment on YouTube.

nodeData.topic: Day 17 · Text 16: Stop speculating, just chant
nodeData.note: Mukunda-mala-stotra 16 · a class by HH Bhakti Dhira Damodara Swami. Kulasekhara tells souls drowning in material existence to put aside their many efforts at knowledge and simply chant and bow to the Lord. Maharaj contrasts the dry, endless path of speculation with bhakti, an ocean of nectar, explains Prabhupada's phrase that Krishna is a compact of love, and tells how Radha and Krishna's love melted into Jagannatha. Questions cover the scriptures as Krishna's manual and how a disciple serves and pleases the guru. Notes are our own summary of the class; tap a bubble's link to hear that moment on YouTube.

nodeData.topic: Day 18 · Text 19: Senses made beautiful by service
nodeData.note: Mukunda-mala-stotra 19 · a class by HH Bhakti Dhira Damodara Swami. King Kulasekhara says the head, eyes, intelligence and tongue become truly beautiful only when they serve Krishna. Maharaj tells the story of the jackal who would not eat a body that never served Krishna, recalls bathing in a dirty Ganga-fed lake, and shows how bhakti transforms devotees like Kubja. In questions he speaks of the spiritual name, accepting chastisement, and preaching to non-devotees. Notes are our own summary of the class; tap a bubble's link to hear that moment on YouTube.

nodeData.topic: Day 19 · Text 20: Ordering every sense to serve
nodeData.note: Mukunda-mala-stotra 20 · a class by HH Bhakti Dhira Damodara Swami. King Kulasekhara commands his tongue, mind, hands, ears, eyes, feet, nose and head to serve Krishna. Maharaj explains each sense with the gopis, the cowherd boys and Sukadeva's verses in the Second Canto, contrasts proud leaders with King Prataparudra sweeping before Jagannatha, and stresses that the mind must be engaged along with the senses. Questions cover bowing on wet ground, honouring a pure devotee's foot-water, mobile phones, the mind and intelligence, and the danger of position. Notes are our own summary of the class; tap a bubble's link to hear that moment on YouTube.

nodeData.topic: Day 20 · Text 21: Practice without remembrance is empty
nodeData.note: Mukunda-mala-stotra 21 · a class by HH Bhakti Dhira Damodara Swami. King Kulasekhara says scripture, vows, pious duties and pilgrimage are worthless without remembering Lord Narayana's lotus feet. Maharaj tells the story of the cobbler and the learned brahmana whose faith Narada tests, and warns against blind following, selfie pilgrimages and austerity done for anything but Krishna. Many questions follow, on office work, Kartika vows, recognising a pure devotee, dharma, and how to approach the spiritual master. Notes are our own summary of the class; tap a bubble's link to hear that moment on YouTube.

nodeData.topic: Day 21 · Text 22: Cupid, leave my heart
nodeData.note: Mukunda-mala-stotra 22 · a class by HH Bhakti Dhira Damodara Swami. King Kulasekhara boldly orders Cupid to leave a mind that now belongs to Mukunda's feet, warning him of Krishna's disc after Lord Shiva has already burned him once. Maharaj explains lust as the all-devouring enemy of Bhagavad-gita 3.37, love of God perverted, and tells how Krishna became Madana-mohana and Radharani Madana-mohana-mohini. The cure is to keep busy in Krishna's service and to care for others, unlike Yayati and Saubhari Muni. Notes are our own summary of the class; tap a bubble's link to hear that moment on YouTube.
